title: REST: constraints and the Richardson model
summary: REST is an architectural style (Roy Fielding, 2000), not a protocol or a standard.

sections.definition: REST is an architectural style (Roy Fielding, 2000), not a protocol or a standard. It defines constraints: client-server, stateless, cacheable, uniform interface, layered system and, optionally, code on demand. The Richardson model measures how well an API meets them, from level 0 to 3.
sections.analogy: REST is like the rules of a public library: each book has a unique location (URI), all of them are requested with the same form (uniform interface), the librarian does not remember your previous visit (stateless), you may photocopy pages that say "copying allowed" (cacheable) and you do not know whether the book comes from the warehouse or another branch (layers).
sections.problem: The constraints exist for a reason: stateless allows scaling, cacheable reduces load, uniform interface makes any client understand any resource, and layers allows putting CDNs, load balancers and gateways in place without the client noticing.
sections.code:wire:
# Nivel 3 (HATEOAS): la respuesta dice qué puedes hacer ahora
GET /v1/pedidos/1093 HTTP/1.1

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/hal+json

{"id":1093,"estado":"pendiente","total":76000,
 "_links":{
   "self":   {"href":"/v1/pedidos/1093"},
   "pagar":  {"href":"/v1/pedidos/1093/pagos","method":"POST"},
   "cancelar":{"href":"/v1/pedidos/1093","method":"DELETE"}}}
sections.code:server:
# FastAPI te lleva naturalmente al nivel 2: recursos + métodos + códigos.
router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1/pedidos", tags=["pedidos"])

@router.get("")                     # colección
@router.post("", status_code=201)   # crear en la colección
@router.get("/{id}")                # elemento
@router.patch("/{id}")
@router.delete("/{id}", status_code=204)
sections.bad:
# Nivel 0: un solo endpoint, todo por POST (estilo RPC/SOAP)
POST /api   {"accion":"obtenerPedido","id":1093}
POST /api   {"accion":"cancelarPedido","id":1093}
sections.good:
# Nivel 2: recursos, métodos y códigos de estado
GET    /v1/pedidos/1093   → 200
DELETE /v1/pedidos/1093   → 204
sections.bridge:typescript: An API client module with getAll, getById, create, update and remove maps almost one to one to a level 2 API. If your module has methods like ejecutarAccion(tipo, payload) against a single endpoint, you are consuming a level 0.
sections.interview: REST is an architectural style defined by Roy Fielding, based on constraints: client-server separation, stateless communication, cacheable responses, a uniform interface (resources identified by URIs, manipulated through representations, self-descriptive messages and hypermedia), a layered system and code on demand as optional. The Richardson maturity model makes it practical: level 0 is a single RPC-style endpoint; level 1 introduces resources with their own URIs; level 2 uses HTTP methods and codes correctly, which is where most of the industry is; and level 3 adds HATEOAS, with links that indicate the possible actions.
sections.myths:
• Believing REST is "HTTP + JSON". You can use HTTP and JSON and not be REST, and REST does not require JSON.
  • Thinking most "REST" APIs comply with full REST. Almost all are at level 2, without HATEOAS.
  • Confusing REST with CRUD. Resources can represent processes (a payment, an approval), not just tables.
